title: packet-xml.c: Use libxml2 for DTD configuration files
description:
Revert a lot of 727dfd5d to restore the code flow of how XML DTD fields are registered to match Flex parser behavior.
However, do a straight replacement of Flex parser behavior with using libxml2 and some of the parsing logic used by 727dfd5d

Ping #20508

notes.body:
I think this is the "right" fix for !20665.  @johnthacker 's initial code for using libxml2's DTD API was the "example code" I needed to complete this (was struggling with some of the "higher level" APIs).
Here's the "debug output" I used to prove the fix.
[new_xml_fields.txt](/uploads/d69bfac49556ba33fcfaa48cb529a2a2/new_xml_fields.txt)[original_xml_fields.txt](/uploads/9ab60b3c6b6959e08a557b910a646638/original_xml_fields.txt)
There are some slight differences in smil.dtd data, but I believe it's acceptable.

Smil.dtd uses DTD parameter entities, are the differences around that or are they handled correctly? I will take a look.

Somewhat unsurprisingly, with this change compared to the state after !20665 the number of instructions and startup time is slightly worse in the case where no XML dissection occurs, but better in the case where all the XML fields have to be loaded. (Either way better than before !20665.) That adds on my box a few milliseconds to the startup time to read an empty file.

It makes `proto_register_xml` once again the slowest of all the protocols to register, and a place I would look to optimize. Most of the added time is spent in `make_xml_hier`. So I think possibly a good sweet spot would be parsing the files and generating the `dtd_build_data_t` at startup, registering the protocol names and handoff information at startup (as with !20665), but doing `make_xml_hier` and the field registration as necessary. That would be eliminating the flex parser and doing somewhat more SAX-based parsing of the elements and attributes at startup in exchange for not needing to parse the files at all later.

Incidentally, for overall startup time the big contributors on Linux for a standard configuration profile are:

1. Loading all the dynamic libraries and their symbols (biggest way to reduce this is to compile without certain dependencies or possibly compile in static versions.)
2. The various "check to see if the hf has legal properties" like `tmp_fld_check_assert` and `proto_check_field_name`
3. Registering of the fields in the big hash map (both the hash calculation and because it gets very large so it causes memory lookup faults)
4. Allocating and increasing the size of the pointer arrays for each protocol's list of hfs.
5. Various parsing of text files

2, 3, and 4 can be reduced by deferring field registration. Nonstandard preferences can greatly increase startup time, particularly some of those that end up pre-calculating cryptographic state based on what's configured in a UAT.

Did you want any of the optimizations as part of this MR or should this be merged and have the optimizations be a separate patch?  The bigger goal of this patch was to eliminate the Flex parsing, I just didn't want too big of a performance hit (it does seem that libxml2 performs slightly worse than our "homegrown solutions", but I'd gladly keep it for future flexibility.

My preference is that we add the fixed here to add callbacks to fully produce the identical `dtd_build_data_t` as the flex based parser, store that (instead of a filename) in the "to be done later" map, and remove all the flex based parsing and call `make_xml_hier` using the `dtd_build_data_t` at the same place as the current master branch.

If this MR reverts all the "call make_xml_hier and register the actual fields later" changes, I will end up wanting to put them back, so it seems like a smaller change to do that.
So the dtd_build_data_t structure should have char* and not the xmlChar* data I was trying to add to keep it in line with the libxml2 API?
Hmm. xmlChar is a typedef for unsigned char. At some point we have to cast it to plain char for the epan API; I don't know if it matters exactly when.

xmlChar is a typedef for unsigned char. For similar reasons, we use uint8_t (which in practice is the same thing, on any system with CHAR_BIT == 8) in some of our code that handles strings of various encodings. On any system with 2's complement signed integer and CHAR_BIT == 8, which is all the platforms we run on, casting between them is perfectly fine and doesn't matter at all. 
libxml2 has a symbol "BAD_CAST" used to convert in order to prevent compiler warnings.

We don't do that - and so we turn off `-Wpointer-sign` (see #20175) because there's probably thousands of cases of converting between plain (and actually signed on many platforms) char and uint8_t.

Huh, on Windows (but nothing else) there seems to be some memory segmentation errors if the xmlChar retrieved from the document are freed with g_free. I wonder exactly what's going on there. Looks like your changes are necessary then.
All of the memory/copying optimizations should have this handled.

Attributes require a parent, but it's not necessarily the last element found (and it's not in smil.dtd), it's the element with name `elem` passed to this function. If you:

1. Check `if g_build_data->last_attribute != NULL && xmlStrcmp(elem, g_build_data->last_attribute->name) == 0`, and add to the existing list only in that case (because there might be two consecutive AttrLists without an element in between, you don't want to add to the list of the last one), and if not
2. Search `g_build_data->elements` backwards from the end and set `el` to the Element `dtd_named_list_t*` such that `xmlStrxmp(elem, el->name) == 0` (because it's not necessarily the last element, though it makes sense to look there first). Then create a `new_attribute` list as before in this case.

Then this version will produce the same results as the flex-based version.

It will fail for any DTD where the Element is defined *after* its AttrList, but we don't have any like that. See also https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#attdecls

> At user option, an XML processor MAY issue a warning if attributes are declared for an element type not itself declared, but this is not an error.

Actually, I guess you don't even really have to search the list of elements, you just have to create a new attribute if `elem` is different from the last one. (It does leak if two AttributeLists are defined for the same Element name in the DTD.)

"When more than one AttlistDecl is provided for a given element type, the contents of all those provided are merged."

So the proper thing to do is to search the list of attributes (starting from the end), and create a new attribute if it's not there. We don't need the last element struct member, just start the search from the end.

Well, the thing is those two arrays are only used for the main protocol and any DTDs that don't register their own protocol. But all the examples do (and then have their own arrays allocated elsewhere.) So actually those two only have 13 and 5 entries.
I agree with @johnthacker that it's not worth presizing the array for ~40 fields (DTDs + main protocol)

Need to call `xmlFreeEnumeration(tree);` (possibly after a NULL check) here to avoid a leak. The default SAX2 handler uses it and then frees it; the parser frees it beforehand if there's no SAX2 parser.

I kind of think libxml2 should really free it either way (but they can't make that change now), though I guess it's possible that some non-default SAX2 handler might not want it freed.

The performance of `register_dtd` is still fairly slow. A lot of that is because of copying the various wmem_maps in order to produce new versions of the elements for the hierarchical (recursive) version where each element has a unique FQN.

The attribute maps are copied just so that they can point to the hfid which is registered. The hfid pointers could be created at registration time, removing the need to copy the maps.

One thing is that the `xml_ns_t` is exposed in packet-xml.h - (since 39515048dccd8b71c0985b329abf0816a1254b19, which was modified since, e.g. by cc893abb25cc568d17ae1afcb4822f521d1f9e30.) My thought is the internal structure of `xml_ns_t` should probably not be exposed in the header, it should be opaque. The two dissectors that access the `xml_frame_t` structure don't access the `xml_ns_t` structure. (There could of course be third party dissectors.) If anything does need to access the structure's members, it should do so through some kind of API call.
Good suggestions.  I'll try to create the hfid fields "more directly" and move the xml_ns_t structure into packet-xml.c

commits_data.title: packet-xml.c: Performance improvements when registering parsed data fields
commits_data.message:
packet-xml.c: Performance improvements when registering parsed data fields

1. The element_names member of the xml_ns_t structure is temporary, but the data it holds is not. And the data it holds is always iterated over and doesn't need indexed access, so convert it to a GList that has faster add/remove of items.  Also it doesn't need to be duplicated when making a fresh object because the previous object data can be iterated over.

2. Make the data parsed from the DTD files wmem_epan_scoped().  That limits the number of duplicate copies of the (string) data made in the post processing of registering hf fields

3. Recursive hierarchy check can be done with a GQueue object for a simple push/pop/iterate check.

4. Make fully_qualified_name a wrapper for a single wmem_strdup_printf call
